text:
sara: @here noticing a sudden spike in DB connection wait times across us-west serving clusters, started ~10:08 UTC. 5xx rates up ~2.3x. thinking we should do a quick sync to triage. logs below.

james: ack. can we do a 15-min ad-hoc? I can grab the bridge.

anika: ping me the link, will pull metrics and traces. suspecting connection pool exhaustion from a bad rollout?

sara: logs snippet:
```
2026-01-07T10:07:58Z ERROR service/generate.go:421 failed to fetch kvcache: dial tcp 10.12.4.7:5432: i/o timeout
2026-01-07T10:08:01Z WARN router/proxy.go:89 upstream 503 serving-node-12
```

li: Query patterns look normal on quick glance, but open connections jumped from avg 120 to 900 in 3m on node12. might be a retry storm from a recent client change.

matt: i've seen a couple of deploys at 09:59 from canary. not sure if related. tagging deploy-bot for more info.

devops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy of service "redwood-gen" v2.14.8 completed at 2026-01-07T09:59:42Z to us-west-2a. No auto-rollback triggered.

sara: ok. proposed quick agenda for the sync:
- 10:10–10:15: confirm blast radius (affected clusters/nodes)
- 10:15–10:20: check deploy overlap and rollback decision
- 10:20–10:23: temporary mitigation (throttle/retry backoff/scale)
- 10:23–10:25: assign follow-ups + handover to oncall

james: bridge: https://meet.redwood.co/adhoc/18492 (pw: rw-sync). jumping in now.

anika: joining, grabbing dashboards: Prometheus: /graph?g0.expr=db_connection_wait_seconds%7Binstance%3D%22node12%22%7D

li: copying a quick command to list active DB connections on host:
```
ssh db-host-7 'psql -c "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = \"active\";'"
```

matt: i'm checking canary logs and will tail the app logs for retry bursts.

sara: @james can you also mute non-essential alerts for the next 10m? reduce noise so we can focus.

james: done: muted alert group "gen-5xx-spikes" for 10m :white_check_mark:

oncall: will take over after 10:25. if we need a rollback, call it and i'll coordinate with infra.

anika: quick note — if it's a retry storm, a short-scale-down of canary traffic + increasing DB max connections isn't ideal long-term. prioritize graceful throttling.

sara: agreed. if we can get a short mitigation (throttle + bump DB connections by 20%) that should buy time for rollback.

li: collecting current connection config: max_connections=500, active 900 -> we are hitting a pool proxy. might need to increase proxy limit or reduce incoming connections.

matt: i see exponential backoffs not firing in v2.14.8 due to a missing env var in the canary. that would explain retries. opening PR to fix retry config: https://git.redwood.co/r/redwood/gen/pull/2541

james: ok team on bridge. starting timeline notes in thread for incident log.

sara: after sync please drop short blurb in #incidents with the summary and follow-ups. I'll also attach the runbook steps we used.

anika: copying runbook extract:
```
Runbook — DB spikes
1) identify spike window and affected nodes
2) mute noisy alerts
3) reduce canary traffic or rollback
4) temporary DB proxy limit increase
5) monitor error rate for 10m
```

matt: mitigation applied: scaled down canary traffic by 60% at 10:13 UTC. DB proxy limit increased to 750 at 10:16 UTC.

li: connections dropped to ~250 after those changes. 5xx rate returning to baseline.

sara: great. taking follow-ups: anika to audit retry config across services, matt to merge fix PR, li to file infra task for proxy autoscale, james to write incident note in #incidents. assigning to oncall for 24h watch.

oncall: acknowledged. will keep an eye and escalate if error rate exceeds 1.5x baseline.

james: incident note posted: https://incidents.redwood.co/2026-01-07-db-conn-spike

sara: thanks everyone. closing ad-hoc sync. :heart:

matt: adding retrospective item to next eng sync: make retry config test part of canary checklist.

anika: +1

sara: end thread.
